A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 34-page versions of the same work. Full-document text and rendering comparisons, including Appendices A–C, establish that differences are confined to the version stamp and three mathematical or algorithmic corrections.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original synthetic experiments measuring BSI-MNL stopping times in Figure 1 and linear maximization oracle runtimes in Table 1.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original synthetic stopping-time and runtime experiments, including Figure 1 and Table 1.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2, line 3 changes the warm-up loop condition from uncertainty ≤ ζw to uncertainty > ζw, making it consistent with the item-selection step. Section 4.1 also replaces the sum in ζw with a minimum. These are localized corrections to initialization; the design oracles, estimation procedure and final stopping rule remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic MNL best-assortment task, random feature and parameter distributions, nonuniform revenues, and N/K configurations. No dataset, task or test scenario is added in the appendices.

E2.justification: Figure 1 and Table 1 retain BSI-MNL-MILP, BSI-MNL-Lift and the brute-force BSI-MNL-Oracle comparator. No comparison method is added, removed or replaced.

E3.justification: Section 5 specifies a factor-of-ten-scaled theoretical warm-up threshold. Although that sentence is unchanged, Section 4.1 changes the referenced expression from a sum to a minimum, tightening the reported warm-up prescription. The PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun; other evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness test, error analysis or case study is added or revised. The appendices continue to supply theoretical supporting material without additional empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 10 independent problem instances/random seeds with one standard deviation. The uncertainty-reporting practice in Section 5, Figure 1 and Table 1 is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 1's curves and error bars and all Table 1 entries are unchanged. For example, at N=200 and K=5, both report MILP runtime 325.60 ± 203.32 seconds and Lift runtime 0.18 ± 0.09 seconds, with exhaustive enumeration marked infeasible.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C.1, Lemma C.3 replace the sum of 1/sqrt(d log(N/δ)) and 1/(B sqrt(λ)) with their minimum. This corrects the warm-up threshold and resulting bound to match the confidence prerequisites in Lemmas 4.2/C.2. The main theorems and remaining proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about the certified MILP oracle, polynomial-time lifted surrogate and instance-dependent sample complexity for best-assortment identification.

C2.justification: The statistical–computational trade-off, small-gap qualification, comparison with item-level gaps and interpretation of the N/K stopping-time trends remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: The corrected ζw formula revises the explicit warm-up hyperparameter prescription needed for reproduction, and Algorithm 2 corrects its loop test. Solver information, numerical tolerances, heuristic scaling and resource-access disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography and novelty positioning relative to earlier MNL and linear-bandit research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 25 May 2026 to v2 dated 26 August 2026. Body prose, terminology, section order and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables and algorithm displays retain their structure, captions, formatting and placement. The mathematical-symbol corrections and version-stamp update introduce no layout reorganization.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects an internally inconsistent warm-up loop and aligns the threshold and Lemma C.3 with the existing confidence conditions. These localized repairs improve mathematical consistency and implementability. The principal contributions and empirical evidence remain unchanged, and no experimental rerun is established.
